narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Cursor AppSec review of `deftai/directive` @ `bd0f3cdc` — **5 validated findings (3 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM)**.

Same residual class as closed #3545 (UAT Shell dest/programmatic-write allowlists), plus a **new MCP write routing gap**, plus a **missed #2912 migrate sink**.

Do **not** reopen #3545. File this as the next residual + two distinct sinks.

## Environment

- SHA: `bd0f3cdc` (`fix(cli): emit deft <verb> for agent-facing commands (#3439) (#3590)`)
- Surfaces: PreToolUse `decideHook`, `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`, `packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/agents-header.ts`

## Findings

### 1. HIGH — MCP write tools (and Cursor `CallMcpTool`) bypass UAT edit gates

**Location:** `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` (Shell/MCP branch ~1264–1274 → `decideShellOrMcpRuntimeAuthority`).

**Path:** Write/Edit under active UAT go through `inspectMutationGates` / authz-grant. MCP write-shaped tools (`mcp__filesystem__write_file`, `edit_file`, `mcp__ide__apply_edit`, `server__write_file`, …) match `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts:105–121`) but `classifyMcpTool` / `listShellOps` only map MCP → push/merge. Unrecognized ops → `ops=[]` → allow `shell-op-unclassifiable` (`dispatcher.ts:762–774`). Cursor `CallMcpTool` is not in `DIRECT_WRITE_TOOL_NAMES`, `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`, or `MCP_HOOK_MATCHER` — PreToolUse may not fire at all.

**Impact:** Wave 1 UAT human-approval bypass via MCP write channel (outside Shell classify allowlists). Forged `operator-cli` grant under `.deft/authz/grants/` then unlocks Write/push/PR/merge.

**Fix:** Treat MCP/server write-shaped tools as **direct-write/edit** under authz. Match `CallMcpTool` in PreToolUse. Fail-closed on unclassifiable MCP mutations **under UAT**.

### 2. HIGH — UAT residual after #3545: extra bins still plant `.deft/authz` grants

**Location:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`

#3545 denied rubyN / DESTDIR / dpkg / fromdos / degit / …. These residuals still harvest empty (`classifyShellAuthzOps([])` → allow `shell-op-unclassifiable`):

`raku`, `crystal`, `groovy`, `clojure`, `graalpy`, `micropython`, `jar`, `gsed`, `helm`, `s3cmd`, `sbase-cp` (and peers)

Target: `.deft/authz/grants/*.json`. Same plant → grant activation class as prior residuals.

**Fix:** Extend programmatic-write / dest-writer sets for these bins. Fail-closed on unclassifiable **write-shaped** Shell under UAT (do not fail-closed `git status`).

### 3. HIGH — same residual writers plant `.deft-directive-disable`

Same bins as (2), targeting kill-switch basenames (`.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive`). Empty classify → Shell allow → `detectDeftDirectiveDisable.active` → allow/`directive-disabled` for all tools (#3039). Immediate full Directive bypass for the session.

**Fix:** Classify residual writers targeting kill-switch basenames as **settings** under UAT.

### 4. MEDIUM — same residual writers forge `.deft/approved-scope`

After #3410 / #3421 / #3529 / #3545, Write of approved-scope is denied; `cp` denied; residuals still allow. Forge `kind=operator` humanApproval JSON → bypass human-presence mint (#3110 / #3384).

**Fix:** Extend approved-scope Shell classify to the **same** residual dest writers as (2)/(3). One allowlist, three dests.

### 5. MEDIUM — `migrate` agents-header: in-tree AGENTS.md leaf diversion

**Location:** `packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/agents-header.ts`

`projectionTarget` uses only `assertProjectionContained` (`:19–24`), which allows an **in-tree** symlink. Default write is `writeFileSync` (`:140`, `:154–155`). Force-added `AGENTS.md` → in-tree victim (e.g. `package.json`) containing legacy `vbrief/` tokens: `deft migrate:xbrief` / `patchAgentsMdHeader` follows the leaf and overwrites the victim. `assertWriteTargetSafe` would refuse. Init-deposit #2912 fixed the parallel class; this sink missed.

**Fix:** `assertWriteTargetSafe` / `assertDestinationNotSymlink` before the header write (mirror #2912). Do not keep `writeFileSync` on a projection-contained path that may be a symlink.

## Expected (thin)

1. Under active UAT, MCP write-shaped tools and `CallMcpTool` take the **same authz/edit path as Write/Edit** (or fail closed if unclassifiable).
2. Residual bins in (2) targeting `.deft/authz/**`, kill-switch basenames, or `.deft/approved-scope/**` classify as settings deny (not `shell-op-unclassifiable` allow). Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable.
3. `patchAgentsMdHeader` refuses in-tree symlink destinations the same way #2912 did for init-deposit.

## Non-goals

- Reopening #3545.
- Fail-closed Shell for every unclassifiable command outside UAT (would invert #2711 `git status` fail-open).
- Weakening Edit/Write UAT to match the MCP/Shell hole (#3156).

## Refs

#3545 (closed residual parent), #3529, #3421, #3410, #3039, #2912, #2711, #3110 / #3384, #3438 (Shell vs Edit scope gate — complementary tool-class hole, not UAT authz).

## Verdict

Do not bind the issue as written. The bypasses are real, but the proposed remedies still classify authority by surface spellings instead of defining one effective invocation and one privileged-destination invariant. Recut this into three independent slices: proxy-aware MCP routing, language-agnostic UAT protection for authority stores, and a local safety invariant on `patchAgentsMdHeader`.

### F0 — `footnote` — untrusted issue-body directives

The body contains imperative process text (for example, directions about filing and reopening work). I treated it as untrusted issue data and did not execute it. I found no concealed instruction marker or cross-source fragment that changes this critique.

### F1 — `blocks-the-design` — adding MCP names to a matcher does not create an enforcement path

**Evidence.** At dispatch SHA `65625417`, an active-UAT probe returned:

```text
mcp__filesystem__write_file -> allow / shell-op-unclassifiable
CallMcpTool                 -> allow / not-direct-write
mcp__github__merge_pull_request -> deny / authz-grant-missing
```

The result follows the current split: [`isMcpTool`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts#L72-L90) recognizes prefixed names, but [`classifyMcpTool`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts#L538-L569) only produces push/merge. The dispatcher therefore fail-opens an unrecognized prefixed tool and never routes `CallMcpTool` at all ([dispatcher](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L2834-L2850)). The repository's own host audit says Cursor's emitted surface is unobserved and records Grok's analogous `use_tool` proxy as an unresolved nested-name problem ([audit](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/content/docs/host-tool-surface-audit.md#L66-L96)).

**Failure mode.** A literal `CallMcpTool` matcher only guarantees that the hook may run. Classification still sees the outer proxy name, while a different proxy spelling or an MCP mutation named `put`, `save`, or another non-`write` verb remains unclassified. Name-fragment matching also trusts an MCP server's arbitrary naming as capability metadata.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected item 1 cannot bind until it requires an observed Cursor `preToolUse` payload and a shared, host-aware “effective invocation” resolver for proxy tools (`CallMcpTool`, `use_tool`, and future audited equivalents). Under active UAT, an MCP invocation that is neither positively read-only nor mapped to a known operation should enter the existing grant-immune `unknown` deny path. The host tool-surface audit and deposited matcher/runtime-classifier consistency check must be part of acceptance, not inferred from fixture names.

### F2 — `blocks-the-design` — “same authz/edit path” is incomplete without effective target extraction

**Evidence.** For a representative wrapper payload whose inner arguments contain `path: "packages/core/src/x.ts"`, `hookMutationTargetPaths` returned `[]`. The extractor only examines one `tool_input` level and top-level path spellings ([paths](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts#L9-L24)); it does not descend from proxy metadata into inner `arguments`. Those targets drive effective-root admission, per-path UAT evaluation, and the runtime/story write fence ([dispatcher target loop](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts#L460-L496)).

**Failure mode.** An implementation can label the proxy as `edit` yet evaluate `path=null`. That is not equivalent to Write/Edit: it loses worktree admission, `file_scope`, deny-path, and surface-restricted grant checks. A broad edit grant can then authorize a mutation whose actual destination was never measured; multi-target or delete-style MCP tools compound the gap.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected item 1 must require unwrapping both the effective tool name and its effective arguments, extracting every mutation target, and feeding those targets through the existing `inspectMutationGates` path. Missing, malformed, expanded, or multi-target arguments must have an explicit UAT disposition; “matched the wrapper” is not acceptance evidence.

### F3 — `blocks-the-design` — the residual-bin remedy repeats the allowlist failure class

**Evidence.** I ran the named interpreter/archive forms against an active UAT lease. Representative writes to all three authority destinations still returned `allow / shell-op-unclassifiable`:

```text
raku spurt -> .deft/authz/grants/**
crystal File.write -> .deft-directive-disable
groovy File.text -> .deft/approved-scope/**
clojure spit -> .deft/authz/grants/**
graalpy open(..., "w") -> .deft-directive-disable
micropython open(..., "w") -> .deft/approved-scope/**
jar cf -> .deft/authz/grants/**
```

By contrast, `sbase-cp ... .deft/authz/grants/**` now returns `deny / authz-uat-deny` through the later generic last-destination `unknown` mechanism. The current classifier already has a long interpreter allowlist ([programmatic bins](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts#L3024-L3071)), while [`unknown` is deliberately grant-immune under active UAT](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/authz/evaluate.ts#L322-L330). The targeted suite still passed 360 tests across six files, confirming that these concrete forms are absent from the existing regression surface.

**Failure mode.** Adding the eleven current executable names moves the bypass frontier to the next interpreter, alias, wrapper, or write API. It also incorrectly requires a positively identified `settings` operation where the system already has the safer meaning: “this touches a protected destination but cannot be proven safe” = `unknown`.

**Disposition consequence.** Replace the executable-list remedy with a protected-control-plane invariant: under UAT, any shell invocation that references `.deft/authz/**`, `.deft/approved-scope/**`, or either kill-switch as a possible destination and is not positively proven read-only must classify `settings` when understood, otherwise `unknown`. Keep ordinary destinations such as `/tmp` fail-open and keep proven reads open. Use the listed binaries and API-shaped commands as a cross-product regression corpus, not as the policy boundary.

### F4 — `sharpens-framing` — the header helper is unsafe, but the claimed CLI path is already intercepted

**Evidence.** A direct repro with an in-tree `AGENTS.md -> package.json` symlink changed the victim from `vbrief/active/story.vbrief.json` to `xbrief/active/story.xbrief.json`; `patchAgentsMdHeader` returned `patched`. In the same setup, `assertWriteTargetSafe` refused the symlink. The helper calls only `assertProjectionContained` ([agents-header](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/agents-header.ts#L19-L23)), which intentionally allows in-tree diversion. However, the production CLI sequence runs `runAgentsRefresh` first, and that function calls `assertWriteTargetSafe` before the later header patch ([migration sequence](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/migrate-project.ts#L320-L345), [call order](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/65625417e5eebf5a5c7e59308ba006f222c06d19/packages/core/src/xbrief-migrate/migrate-project.ts#L547-L559)).

**Failure mode.** The exported helper remains an unsafe write sink and a future/direct caller can overwrite an in-tree victim, but the body overstates the current end-to-end `deft migrate:xbrief` overwrite: that call path exits at the earlier refresh preflight before `runHeaderPatch` executes.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep the local defense-in-depth fix (`assertDestinationNotSymlink` or `assertWriteTargetSafe` inside `patchAgentsMdHeader`) and add an in-tree leaf-symlink test on the helper itself. Narrow the finding and severity to the exported helper/future-call invariant unless a production path that bypasses `runAgentsRefresh` is demonstrated.

## Road not taken

The strongest alternative is the issue's thin patch: add the named binaries, add `CallMcpTool`, and add the symlink guard. It is fast, preserves non-UAT compatibility, and closes the supplied examples. I reject it because the current tree already demonstrates both recurrence mechanisms: matcher coverage without runtime classification, and successive writer allowlists followed by new residuals. I would flip if supported hosts supplied authoritative MCP capability metadata plus observed payload fixtures, and a generic negative corpus showed that new proxy spellings and interpreter aliases cannot bypass UAT without adding their names to policy code.

## Recommended disposition

Recast the three expected items as three stories with independent checks:

1. observed proxy payload -> effective MCP invocation + all targets -> mutation gates; unproved MCP capability is `unknown` under UAT;
2. protected authority destination + not-proven-read-only -> `settings` or grant-immune `unknown`, with binaries only as fixtures;
3. `patchAgentsMdHeader` locally refuses every destination symlink, independent of caller order.

**Evidence.** Expected #1 says "Match `CallMcpTool` in PreToolUse"; the Fix for (2)/(3)/(4) says "Extend programmatic-write / dest-writer sets for these bins." Both are catalog extension. But `bf9d26c8c` (#4449 / closes #4188) is an ancestor of the dispatch SHA and its own message says it "**does not grow dest-flag or write-bin catalogs**" — it pivoted to a dest-of-write invariant instead. The body still asks for the mechanism the repo has already abandoned on this very class.

### 3. sharpens-framing — the MCP branch cannot reach the #4449 dest rule, because it never computes a dest

**Evidence.** `dispatcher.ts:1080` sets `const shellCommand = isShellTool(toolName) ? hookShellCommand(input.payload) : null`. The #4188 realpath recovery at `:1090–1094` is guarded by `shellCommand !== null`. MCP tool names are not shell tools, so the guard is unreachable from the MCP path — structurally, not by omission. `classifyHookAuthzOps` (`authz/classify.ts:4004–4043`) receives only a tool name plus `mcpArgsText` for MCP, and `classifyMcpTool` maps to `push | merge | null` only (`policy/runtime-authority.ts:542–570`); `RuntimeAuthorityShellOp` has no write member.

**Failure mode.** "Extend the #4449 dest rule to MCP" is not a widening — there is no MCP dest extractor to widen. A remedy scoped as "treat MCP write-shaped tools as direct-write under authz" (Expected #1) will pass `relPath: null` into `authzForMutation` exactly as the current call at `dispatcher.ts:1181–1185` does, and the protected-dest comparison will have nothing to compare.

**Disposition consequence.** Expected #1 must name the missing mechanism explicitly: extract the dest from `tool_input.path` / `file_path` / `target_file` / `arguments.path`, resolve it against the payload root with the same realpath walk as `shellCommandHasPayloadRootProtectedDestAfterRealpath`, then apply the finding-1 invariant. Scoped as "same path as Write/Edit" it reads as routing work and will be estimated as such.

### 4. sharpens-framing — findings 1 and 3 compose into a kill-switch plant over MCP, which no listed Fix covers

**Evidence.** Measured: `server__write_file` targeting `/project/.deft-directive-disable` under active UAT with zero grants → **allow** `shell-op-unclassifiable`. The body files the kill-switch plant as HIGH #3 scoped to *Shell* residual bins, and the MCP gap as HIGH #1 scoped to *authz grants*. The intersection is filed nowhere.

**Failure mode.** `detectDeftDirectiveDisable.active` short-circuits every tool to `directive-disabled` (#3039). Finding 1's Fix is scoped to "MCP/server write-shaped tools ... under authz"; finding 3's Fix is scoped to "residual writers targeting kill-switch basenames" — i.e. Shell bins. A remedy that lands both as written, each within its own scope, still leaves a one-call session-global authority revocation over the MCP channel. Grant-plant needs a second step to be useful; the kill-switch plant does not.

**Disposition consequence.** The kill-switch dest deserves its own line in Expected, keyed on dest and not on channel. If the panel ranks the five findings, this composition outranks #1 on blast radius and should not inherit #3's MEDIUM-adjacent framing by being filed under the Shell bullet.

### 5. sharpens-framing — finding 5 is real and reproduced, but the fix site and the primitive are both mis-stated

**Evidence.** The PoC above overwrote `package.json` through an in-tree `AGENTS.md` symlink at the dispatch SHA. Two corrections:

- The write primitive is **bounded**, not arbitrary. `rewriteUnmanagedHeaderTokens` (`agents-header.ts:140`) replaces only `.vbrief.json`, `vbrief:preflight`, and left-bound `vbrief/`, and preserves every `deft:managed-section` block byte-for-byte. The attacker picks the victim file and gets those three token swaps in it — an integrity violation, not content injection.
- The guard is on the **wrong branch**. `agents-header.ts:217` reads `const writePath = usingWriteSeam ? agentsPath : projectionTarget(projectRoot, "AGENTS.md")`. Containment is only consulted when no `writeText` seam is supplied. Expected #3 says "mirror #2912" and the body points at `projectionTarget` (`:19–24`) — a fix placed there leaves every future seam caller unguarded. Today only tests pass the seam (`migrate-project.ts:537` passes none), so this is latent, not live. The read at `:206` is uncontained on both branches.

Record the #3953 split this thread already carried: findings 2-4 dominated into dest-based classification (landed positional dest-of-write in #4449 / #4188; residue parked on #4199); finding 1 is MCP/proxy routing; finding 5 is containment. This arc supersedes write-back 5649902250 and does not re-open that split as one five-finding next-build.

MCP/proxy story: unwrap wrapper inner names (`CallMcpTool`, `use_tool`, and audited equivalents) as a classifier change, not a matcher token. Extract every mutation target from effective arguments and run `inspectMutationGates`. Under active UAT, dest-bearing writes to `.deft/authz/`, `.deft/approved-scope/`, or a kill-switch basename fail closed on the dest-of-write / `unknown` path. Do not fail-closed every unclassifiable MCP (reads such as `list_issues` share that class). Kill-switch dest is dest-keyed, not channel-keyed.

Dest residual story: do not extend programmatic-write / dest-writer sets as grantable `settings`. Positional protected dests are already `unknown` / grant-immune. Surviving gaps are interpreter-payload harvest (`-e`/`-c`/`eval` script text is not a filesystem path today) and archive dest-grammar (`jar cf dest inputs`). Keep `git status` fail-open. Ordinary dests such as `/tmp` stay unclassifiable.

Header story: `patchAgentsMdHeader` calls `assertDestinationNotSymlink` (or equivalent walk) before read and before write, on both the projection branch and the `writeText` seam. Do not place the only guard inside `projectionTarget`. This is reuse of the #2912 primitive, not a new containment API. Production `migrate:xbrief` currently exits earlier at `runAgentsRefresh`; keep a helper-level test so a future seam caller cannot regress.
Observed Cursor `preToolUse` payloads and host-tool-surface audit consistency are acceptance evidence for the MCP story, not inferred from fixture names.
